question: Which of the following is always true for non-zero vectors $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$?
explanation:
$|\vec{a} - \vec{b}|^2 = (\vec{a} - \vec{b})\cdot(\vec{a} - \vec{b}) = |\vec{a}|^2 + |\vec{b}|^2 - 2 \vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}$

So, Option D is false unless $\vec{a},\vec{b}$ anti-parallel.

For Option C:

$|\vec{a} - \vec{b}|^2 + 4(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}) = |\vec{a}|^2 + |\vec{b}|^2 - 2\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} + 4\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}$

$= |\vec{a}|^2 + |\vec{b}|^2 + 2 \vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}$

which is $(|\vec{a}| + |\vec{b}|)^2$. So Option C is always true.
